correctness.rationale: In the specified orthonormal-coordinate realization the face free generators are exactly the roots annihilated by a supporting objective. Rank two in a simple triangle-free graph forces two edges, and their Gram area squared is 3 for intersecting edges and 4 otherwise. A fixed pair yields one face per chamber of the contracted arrangement. A wedge collapses to a universal vertex; a disjoint pair collapses to two adjacent universal vertices, because in a complete bipartite graph each merged block includes both types of vertices. The rest remains a biclique. The joins give acyclic-orientation counts B2 and 2B3, respectively; the pairs themselves have multiplicities p·C(q,2), q·C(p,2), and 2·C(p,2)·C(q,2). This gives exactly the asserted formulas. At fixed p the two leading coefficients have common factor p!·C(q,2)·(p+1)^(q−2) and multipliers p and p(p−1); the other wedge has base p. This checks the frequency and mean. B2(0,b)=2^b, B2(1,b)=2·3^b and B3(0,b)=3^b give the thin two-vertex formulas, including four squares and eight rhombi at p=q=2. The seven-case checker was inspected, not executed; it is finite corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The distinction between the unrefined f-vector and the metric histogram is real, but the strongest prior gives the count separately for the exact flat indexing each metric class, before summation. The complete claimed histogram is a direct evaluation of those existing contributions using rank-two incidence and two elementary join substitutions; the limit then follows by keeping the unique largest base in a finite standard coloring sum. This is demonstrated coverage by implication, not a claim that a published table explicitly prints the area split.
residual_risks: An explicitly printed earlier metric histogram was not located; the finding of prior coverage rests on the exact specialization above, not exhaustive priority attribution.
